Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
357 AM EST Mon Nov 23 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Have added mention of some patchy dense fog across the central
Virginia Piedmont into portions of northern Virginia and
southern Maryland. For the Thanksgiving Day system, the trend
has been further to the west which limits the mountain snow
potential. However, strong winds and soaking rains remain on
track at this juncture.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Mild today with spotty showers before turning cooler by
  Tuesday.

- 2) East Coast storm to bring heavy rain and strong winds to
  the area on Thanksgiving Day.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Mild today with spotty showers before turning
cooler by Tuesday.

The latest surface analysis places the main area of low pressure
just south of Cape Cod while attaching to a weaker low off the
coast of North Carolina. Additionally, looming off to the west
is a cold front currently moving across Lake Erie down into the
Tennessee and Ohio Valleys. The local area is largely sandwiched
in between these two synoptic features. Saturated low levels of
the atmosphere has fostered the development of patchy dense fog
and some stratus. This is particularly the case from the 
central Virginia Piedmont eastward into southern Maryland.
Hourly observations over these locations show visibilities
waffling between 1/4 to 1/2 mile and up to 1 to 2 miles. The
intermittent and sporadic nature of this fog suggests Dense Fog
Advisories will not be needed, but will continue to monitor.

Today will be the mildest day of the week with highs pushing
into the 60s to low 70s. The lone exception would be the
mountains which range from the upper 40s to 50s. The upstream
cold front is slated to move across the region later this
morning. Some upslope aided rain showers are possible along and
west of the Alleghenies, with even some spotty showers leaking
off to the east. However, chances east of the terrain are 
mainly being held at 20 to 30 percent. The real change in the
pattern does not take place until the evening as a secondary
surge arrives. This ushers in a period of brisk winds along with
falling temperatures and dew points. The result is a return of
seasonably cold overnight conditions. Tonight's lows will mainly
be in the 30s east of the Blue Ridge, with mid/upper 20s off to
the west.

The temperature forecast for Tuesday and Wednesday are almost 
mirror images of one another. Daily highs range from the mid 40s
to mid 50s, locally a bit cooler in the mountains. Between the 
two days, Tuesday will provide ample sunshine as a broad surface
high tracks from the Midwest. By Tuesday night, a stout 1042-mb
ridge sits across New England which will make for a cold night 
over the local area. Forecast lows fall into the mid teens to 
mid 20s. For those along and east of I-95, upper 20s to near 
freezing temperatures are more likely. Heading into Wednesday, 
skies will cloud up through the day ahead of the potent 
Thanksgiving Day system. Any impacts largely hold off until 
Wednesday night as northeasterly winds pick up in earnest. 
Although timing varies between models, gusty showers are 
forecast to lift northward across the area overnight. For more 
information on this storm, check out Key Message 2 (below).


KEY MESSAGE 2...East Coast storm to bring heavy rain and strong
winds to the area on Thanksgiving Day.

Model trends since yesterday have shown upper trough over the mid-
section of the country Wednesday digging further south and taking on 
a more negatively tilt, which results in low pressure along the 
Southeast U.S. coast lifting slower to the north and taking on a 
more inland track. This results in heavier rain and stronger winds 
farther inland, and increases the risk of coastal flooding given a 
Full Moon on Tuesday. The more inland sfc low track also increases 
the risk of a low-topped convective line capable of producing 
damaging winds, particularly across the climatological favored areas 
of King George County and southern Maryland south of US-50.

Latest EPS output shows 100% prob of 1" of rain everywhere and 30% 
to 50% prob of 2" or more south of I-66 and US-50. Winds have also 
shown a marked increase with gusts of 40-55 mph likely across much 
of the area and gusts as high as 70 mph along the Chesapeake Bay and 
higher elevations due to an intense 925 mb easterly jet of 70kt. The 
risk of coastal flooding also seems to be increasing due to the 
strong onshore flow combined with high astronomical tides 
associated with a Full Moon Tuesday. 

The storm system departs the local area early Fri morning with 
steady rain ending, with showers turning into snow showers across 
the mountains and broken stratocumulus and gusty WSW winds across 
the rest of the area. The low-level flow does not look particularly 
favorable for a long duration upslope snow event across the 
mountains at this time.

&&

.AVIATION /07Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Some lingering restrictions are noted at KDCA, KBWI, and KMTN
early this morning. This is due to some low clouds and patchy
fog which have begun to materialize. Based on nearby
observations, these reductions in visibility have been somewhat
intermittent in nature. Will continue to advertise such issues
through 12Z before the cold front to the west moves through.
While a few showers are possible today, do not anticipate any
restrictions with these. Expect prevailing northwesterlies today
with gusts picking up to around 20 knots this evening. 

VFR conditions continue into Tuesday and Wednesday as stout high
pressure builds to the north. Winds in turn become northerly 
for Tuesday before shifting to northeasterly Tuesday night into 
Wednesday. Any sub-VFR conditions should hold off until 
Wednesday night as a potent system impacts the region into 
Thanksgiving Day. Overnight northeasterly gusts begin to 
approach 25 to 30 knots ahead of daybreak.

Strong East Coast storm to bring significant travel impacts to 
aviation Thanksgiving Day with heavy rain, IFR flight restrictions, 
wind gusts of 35-45 kt, and strong LLWS. Rain ends early on Fri, but 
MVFR cigs from broken stratocu and gusty WSW winds to continue into 
Saturday.

&&

.MARINE...
After a period of lighter winds over the local waterways, this
break will come to an end by this evening. A cold front off to
the west is forecast to move across the waters this morning. A
stronger north to northeasterly surge moves in this evening
with gusts increasing to 20 to 30 knots into tonight and the
first half of Tuesday. Small Craft Advisories will be needed for
this large uptick in the winds. The northerly winds remain
elevated through the remainder of Tuesday before winds turn more
northeasterly by Wednesday. Additional advisories will likely be
needed as well. Ahead of the strong system arriving for 
Thanksgiving Day, northeasterlies begin to approach near gale
levels on Wednesday night.

High likelihood of gale force winds Thu and even a low of risk of 
storm force winds. High end SCA to low end gale force winds are
expected for Friday.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
As coastal low pressure exits out to sea, a cold front off to the
west will track through this morning. Winds gradually pick up in
intensity this evening into the night. This brings in cooler 
weather for the week, but also lower daytime humidities on Tuesday.
A stronger coastal system is expected to bring wet and windy 
conditions to the region Wednesday into Thanksgiving Day. There is
increasing confidence this brings wetting rains to the entire
area. Gusty winds persist into Friday before high pressure
approaches from the west by the weekend.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Relatively light winds today may allow for tides to elevate 
somewhat, resulting in action stages at vulnerable sites like 
Annapolis, particularly late this afternoon. Thereafter, strong
offshore flow will result in decreasing tides tonight into 
Tuesday.

A stronger coastal low pressure area will likely move up the 
Eastern Seaboard Wednesday into Thanksgiving Day. Depending on 
the evolution and track, tide levels may rise once again. 
Current model progs vary widely from abnormally low tides to 
moderate tidal flooding due to uncertainty in exact wind 
direction/magnitude/low track.

&&

.LWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
DC...None.
MD...None.
VA...None.
WV...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$
